title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: Singapore lawyers going global
sections.summary: Asia Pacific legal services are projected to grow 5.5% yearly from 2014 to 2019, and "Lawyers Go Global" supports Singapore lawyers overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Legal services in the Asia Pacific region are projected to grow at 5.5% per year between 2014 and 2019, outpacing the annual global rate of 3.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The new initiative called "Lawyers Go Global" seeks to support positioning Singapore lawyers with the competitive edge through overseas trips, training, branding and marketing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, "many multinational corporations (MNCs) are based in Singapore and use Singapore lawyers for their regional transactions." In fact, Singapore is the top Asian location for MNCs to set up regional headquarters, with about 46%, compared to 37% in Hong Kong.

sections.label: Singapore international arbitration and SICC
sections.summary: Singapore was first major arbitration centre to offer specialised international arbitration rules, and the SICC gives investors a sophisticated judicial forum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, in January last year, in recognition of the different interests that may arise in international arbitration disputes, Singapore was the first major arbitration centre to offer specialised rules for international arbitration, on top of the more general rules for commercial arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC), as Bloomberg described it, "gives global investors in South and Southeast Asia a judicial forum with international legal sophistication that can rival any in the world." Its unique procedure is also specially adapted for complex commercial cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So that Singapore may continue to expand as a legal hub, what further measures will MinLaw roll out to make the Singapore firms and Singapore-based lawyers relevant to the growing opportunities in ASEAN, Asia and the world?

sections.label: Legal sector transformation and CFE
sections.summary: The legal sector joined the industry transformation exercise, with a CFE Legal and Accounting Working Group set up to study future growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge MinLaw to support and endorse these standards, to carry this forward and across the entire community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I was happy to note that the legal sector has been involved in the industry transformation exercise and the CFE Legal and Accounting Working Group was set up to look into the future growth of the legal and accounting sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What have been the developments and achievements following the recommendations?

sections.label: Supporting Singapore lawyers and law practices
sections.summary: Over 5,000 qualified lawyers practise in Singapore, and the Ministry is asked how it will support lawyers and small and medium-sized law practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Singapore Bar is steadily growing with more than 5,000 qualified lawyers currently in practice and with the Courts and the Ministry enhancing various services to the public, including enhancement of pro bono schemes and reforms in the Family Justice system as well as placing Singapore as an international legal hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, how will the Ministry support Singapore lawyers and Singapore law practices, especially the small and medium-sized law practices, to be ready for the future?

sections.label: Reviewing Small Claims Tribunal jurisdiction
sections.summary: The speaker asks MinLaw to review the Small Claims Tribunal's jurisdiction so more people can get economical orders for contractual claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I have spoken on this before and I am raising this again to MinLaw.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I hope MinLaw will seriously look into reviewing the jurisdiction of the Small Claims Tribunal (SCT) so that more people can have economical and expedient orders in judgment for their contractual claims.

sections.label: Model ASEAN Extradition Treaty
sections.summary: Ms Indranee Rajah told the House a model ASEAN Extradition Treaty was being worked on as a template for bilateral arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In September 2016, Senior Minister of State Ms Indranee Rajah told the House that as far as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was concerned, there was a model ASEAN Extradition Treaty being worked on, which would function as a sort of template to enable ASEAN members to enter bilateral arrangements.

sections.label: Roach bank robbery extradition
sections.summary: Roach, suspected of a July 2016 Singapore bank robbery, was arrested in Thailand and is being extradited from London to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Roach was suspected of committing a bank robbery in Singapore in July 2016, one-and-a-half years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He escaped to our ASEAN neighbour, Thailand, was arrested and convicted of other offences under Thai law and is only now being extradited from London to Singapore because he was being deported from Thailand to his home country, Canada, via London.

sections.label: Singapore extradition arrangements countries
sections.summary: Singapore has arrangements with 40 declared Commonwealth countries and bilateral agreements with the US, Germany and Hong Kong, totalling 43 of nearly 200 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore has arrangements with 40 declared Commonwealth countries, as well as bilateral agreements with the US, Germany and Hong Kong, which makes only 43 out of nearly 200 countries.

sections.label: Interstate disputes and international law
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on interstate international law disputes and notes the Permanent Court of Arbitration's land dispute resolution aided KL-Singapore High Speed Rail work.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry update us on our current interstate international law disputes and if public international law remains exclusively important for Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We called in the Permanent Court of Arbitration that administered the land dispute resolution as it is the amicable enforcement of this award that helped to pave the way for us to work with our immediate neighbour on the Kuala Lumpur (KL)-Singapore High Speed Rail Network as well.

sections.label: Public Trustee small estate administration
sections.summary: The Public Trustee may directly administer a deceased person's estate not exceeding $50,000 in value without going to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Presently, the Public Trustee may directly administer the estate of deceased persons where the value of the estate does not exceed $50,000, without going to Court.

sections.label: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal
sections.summary: The Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal, set up in March 2015, hears intractable neighbour disputes within the same building or 100 metres, with about 79 cases as of July 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal was set up in March 2015 to hear cases involving intractable disputes between neighbours after all efforts, including community mediation, have been exhausted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) website, about 79 cases have been heard by the Tribunal as of July 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, this Tribunal is only able to deal with disputes involving neighbours living within the same building or within 100 metres of each other, and where there has been some form of unreasonable interference by the neighbour.

sections.label: Tribunal mandatory treatment orders question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Tribunal can be empowered, within its jurisdiction, to issue mandatory treatment orders against persons found mentally unstable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If it is within their jurisdiction, can the Tribunal be empowered to issue mandatory treatment orders against any person found to be mentally unstable?

sections.label: Legal aid qualifying tests
sections.summary: To qualify for legal aid, Singaporeans must pass a means test showing need and a merits test showing a good claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to qualify for legal aid, Singaporeans will need to pass two tests: the means test to show that they are needy; and the merits test to show that they have a good claim.

sections.label: Arbitration clauses and legal aid
sections.summary: Arbitration clauses in standard form contracts may keep a needy Singaporean from pressing a meritorious claim, as legal aid does not cover arbitration costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In many standard form contracts that Singaporeans enter into, such as insurance policies, there are contractual requirements that the parties go to arbitration in the event of a dispute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are many good reasons why an insurance company that drafts the policy would want such an arbitration clause, but one effect of such a clause is that it may keep a needy Singaporean from pressing a meritorious claim in the event of a dispute, since legal aid currently does not cover the cost of arbitration proceedings.

sections.label: Revising means test threshold
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry plans to revise the legal aid means test threshold to cover a similar proportion of Singaporeans as incomes rise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have any plans to revise the means test threshold for legal aid, so as to cover a similar proportion of Singaporeans, even though average incomes are rising over time?

sections.label: Reviewing means test criteria
sections.summary: Indranee Rajah said the means test and qualifying criteria will be reviewed and updated, and gave 2017 pass rates for both tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah replied that they will review and update the means test and qualifying criteria to ensure access to justice for those of limited means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2017, 92% of applications passed the means test, while 87% passed the merits test.

sections.label: Affordable legal costs, enforcement
sections.summary: The aim is to keep legal costs affordable and reduce civil proceedings complexity, with measures to strengthen enforcement of civil judgments being studied and public consultation likely later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The aim is to keep legal costs affordable and to reduce the complexity of civil proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We are also studying measures to strengthen the enforcement of civil judgments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Public consultation is likely to take place later this year.

sections.label: Committee on family justice reforms
sections.summary: A committee with MSF and the Family Justice Courts was set up, its report will be out later this year, and the Ministry will act on it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To build on these positive reforms, my Ministry has set up a committee with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) as well as Family Justice Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The report will be out later this year, and we will act on it.

sections.label: Cross-border mediation enforcement work
sections.summary: A MinLaw Director chaired work completing a draft Convention and amended Model Law for cross-border enforcement of mediated international commercial settlement agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Under the chairmanship of a MinLaw Director, we have completed work on both a draft Convention and amended Model Law that will provide for the cross-border enforcement of international commercial settlement agreements resulting from mediation.

sections.label: SIAC and SIMC case growth
sections.summary: SIAC cases rose from 99 to 343 between 2008 and 2016, and SIMC signed MOUs with Chinese bodies in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SIAC, for example, saw within 2008 and 2016, in those eight years, a three-fold increase in cases, from 99 to 343.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The total sum in disputes for new cases filed in 2016 hit S$17 billion, and 80% of those cases were international in nature.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It had 22 cases filed in 2017, it now has 42 cases so far, and it was only established three years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For example, in 2017, last year, SIMC signed memorandums of understanding (MOUs) with the Mediation Center of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade/China Chamber of International Commerce, and the Hangzhou Arbitration Commission.

sections.label: Maxwell Chambers expansion
sections.summary: The announced Maxwell Chambers expansion is on track for completion next year, adding 120,000 square feet and tripling its current size.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Last year, we announced that we will be expanding Maxwell Chambers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They are on track to be completed by next year and that will add 120,000 square feet of floor space and it will triple Maxwell Chambers' current size.

sections.label: SLA land use and GeoWorks
sections.summary: SLA will discuss Joo Chiat buildings with relevant agencies, and is building geospatial capabilities through GeoWorks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One example is the Jalan Bukit Merah Viaduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Edwin Tong had a specific question on Joo Chiat's "iconic" buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I will ask SLA to discuss the matter with the relevant agencies because the policy on this matter is with the Ministry of National Development (MND), so they will have to decide what land use they have planned for and we will see what can be done.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As regards the Smart Nation agenda, SLA is also building up Singapore's geospatial capabilities through what we call GeoWorks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Many of them are SMEs or individuals, and they create business opportunities through the use of location-based technologies.

sections.label: Access to legal aid
sections.summary: The Ministry monitors civil and criminal legal aid schemes and will enhance them to ensure access to justice for the less able.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Advancing access to justice is one of my Ministry's core missions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We regularly monitor the civil and criminal legal aid schemes and will enhance them where necessary to ensure access to justice for those less able to fend for themselves.

sections.label: Means test review
sections.summary: The means test is being reviewed so more Singaporeans can be helped, with details to be announced later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Louis Ng asked if we would review our means test, so that more Singaporeans can be helped.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are doing so and will announce details when ready later this year.

sections.label: Legal aid for court matters
sections.summary: Legal aid covers matters litigated in Court, including related alternative dispute resolution proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Legal aid is provided in respect of matters which may be litigated in Court, including related alternative dispute resolution (ADR) proceedings.

sections.label: Funding for CLAS and LSPBS
sections.summary: Since 2015 the Government gave close to $6 million to LSPBS, letting CLAS help almost four times as many applicants in 2017 as before 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since 2015, the Government has provided close to $6 million to the Law Society Pro Bono Services (LSPBS), enabling CLAS to help almost four times as many applicants in 2017, compared to pre-2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The application processing time has been significantly shortened after a direct phone-link between CLAS and Prisons was installed in March 2017.

sections.label: Firms taking CLAS cases
sections.summary: In the past three years, over 20 firms signed MOUs and took on over 600 CLAS cases in total.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the past three years, over 20 firms have signed MOUs and taken on over 600 CLAS cases in total.

sections.label: Restructuring cases filed in Singapore
sections.summary: Since May 2017, more than 15 restructuring cases have been filed with the Singapore Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since May 2017, more than 15 restructuring cases have been filed with the Singapore Courts.

sections.label: Infrastructure Office platform purpose
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Office is intended to connect infrastructure stakeholders, enable information exchange on Asian infrastructure opportunities, facilitate investments and financing, and help infrastructure players access these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Infrastructure Office is intended to be a platform to connect infrastructure stakeholders, enable information exchange on infrastructure opportunities in Asia, facilitate infrastructure investments and financing, and help infrastructure players, including professional services providers, access these opportunities.

sections.label: Law practices adopting technology
sections.summary: About 100 Singapore law practices benefited and adopted over 100 technology solutions, and the Lawyers Go Global programme was launched in February with the Law Society and IE Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: About 100 Singapore law practices have benefited and adopted over 100 technology solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The "Lawyers Go Global" programme was launched in February, together with the Law Society and International Enterprise (IE) Singapore.

sections.label: Singaporean lawyers receiving award
sections.summary: 44 Singaporean lawyers have received the award to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To date, 44 Singaporean lawyers have received the award.

sections.label: International cooperation against transnational crime
sections.summary: The Ministry is committed to international cooperation against transnational crime, with special extradition arrangements with Malaysia and Brunei and negotiations for a Model ASEAN extradition treaty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: My Ministry is committed to facilitating greater international cooperation to combat transnational crime, in accordance with our domestic laws and international obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Within ASEAN, there is no ASEAN-wide initiative for the mutual recognition of arrest warrants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, Singapore has special extradition arrangements with Malaysia and Brunei, given our shared common law tradition and close relationship, which allow for the swift surrender of fugitives based on the recognition of arrest warrants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At present, Singapore is actively engaged in negotiations for a Model ASEAN extradition treaty, as Ms Sylvia Lim noted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As Ms Sylvia Lim acknowledges, our existing extradition network extends to 43 jurisdictions across the globe, including major jurisdictions, such as the US.
